folded: the Callables precision row's justification split from Atoms
and stated honestly -- identity not captures, Separating only while
fz-kdt.127's shape compiles on no path, re-judge if 127 lands; the
axis_erases PerPosition arm made axis-exhaustive. Gate lib 1558/0/5,
cli 24/0, aot 1/0, matrix 446/0/9).

THE P1 IT FIXES (live at base, source-only, ALL THREE doors --
refuter confirmed AOT red too): annotation-based multi-clause
dispatch on tagged tuples always took the first clause
(dispatch_annotated_tuple_tag_clauses: base 1 1 2 2, head 1 2 1 2 =
Elixir oracle; two more refuter-built reproducers confirmed:
reduce-into-annotated-clauses and difference-typed fallthrough).

WHAT LANDED (one commit, the hard constraint honored):
tuple_arities -> TupleShapes (one shape per Descr clause, per-position
RuntimeTypePredicate recursion, exact=false degrades to arity-only on
multi-pos/neg clauses -- degradation single-sourced through is_exact,
refuter-verified all four consumers); RuntimeTestAxis table with
AxisPrecision {Separating, Erasing, PerPosition} -- ALL lattice ops
folded onto it, lowerings decide axes by exhaustive match (invariant
by compilation; two constructive gates); identity-preserving callable
erasure at EVERY depth, positive polarity only (neg-sig polarity flip
verified; neg tuple clauses degrade the axis first); ONE native
emitter (runtime_test.rs, RuntimeTestEmitter trait, prim+receive as
impls -- the fz-kdt.134 fold, -775 lines of duplication);
delivered_tuple_field_arity REPAIRED to emit_delivered_tuple_test
(fz-kdt.133 -- probed unreachable today, 0/1783 lowerings, kept
correct-by-construction); nested tuple schema ids; the fz-kdt.135
tripwire FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP (Lowered-vs-Full re-ask;
baseline 7 fixtures/268 hits, ALL nested-list = fz-kdt.132's shape;
CANNOT see list-element escapes -- scope corrected on 135); the
Scope-A carve-out in ONE function (lowering_tests_position: a
list-bearing position is untested, therefore overlapping AND erasing
-- what a lowering declines to ask, a seat may not claim).

REFUTER VERIFICATION (19 probes x 12 configurations each): three
doors AGREE everywhere; receive stays source-ordered (4-clause
nested-payload probe byte-identical to base and Elixir); the
enum_predicate_search reseat sound on all doors under stress+LIFO;
arities() derivation value-identical (transport/destination-passing
byte-neutral); canon exactly 4 movers (predicate lens 28-line seat
correction + three receive_* arms-become-live; a naive diff shows a
5th -- enum_reduce_halt_arm_order's 166 lines are the fixture's OWN
comment edit shifting lambda byte-offsets, isolated and cleared);
inventory 4929->4971 (+42 = dbg/fz_dbg_value 1->8 on three fixtures,
the 2^arity product = fz-kdt.140); FIFO/LIFO lenses byte-identical,
census 3, corpus stdout 0/1168; 19-escape census byte-identical
(retires zero -- 107's alone); budget headers re-priced and measured
true (fz-kdt.139 confirmed: nothing enforces them).

GATES REWRITTEN with reasoning inverted: fz-kdt.118's headline
REVERSED (narrow twin becomes an honest 2-arm Dispatch);
distinguishable_arms seats NARROW first now that questions differ;
the indistinguishable carve-out gate re-homed on a genuinely
inseparable pair (list elements) with a questions-equal assertion.

RESIDUE RECORDED: F2 = the fixed P1's verbatim twin one axis over
(clause {:a,[integer]} vs {:a,integer} prints 1 1 -- pre-existing,
the authorized Scope-A carve-out; filed on fz-kdt.138 as its
acceptance reproducer); F3 KindEvidence::Opaque answers 0 to a finite
callable test (base-preserved, nested positions safe); F4 interp/
emitter allow_other_structs disagreement (dead: sole producer
hard-codes false); F5 receive-door schema-registration coverage rests
on MakeTuple (0 live occurrences) + closure-in-message probes crash
identically at base (fz-kdt.130's family, noted there). Scope B =
fz-kdt.138 (blocked by fz-kdt.132).

comments.text:
BUILT at 533089cd0 (2026-09-01), one commit, all six spec items plus the gate list. Not closed -- left for the review round.

Everything the spec predicted reproduced, to the number: canon 4 movers (the predicate lens plus three receive fixtures), inventory 4929 -> 4971 with the +42 exactly the three receive fixtures' dbg specs going 1 -> 8 per function, the 19-escape census unmoved, the FIFO/LIFO census still at 3.

Full record is in the commit message. Numbers: lib 1558/0/5 (base 1546, +12 gates), cli 24/0, matrix 446/0/9 (base 443, +3 doors), 584-fixture interp+JIT sweep 0 movers besides the new fixture, AOT green on every canon mover, four lenses byte-identical FIFO vs LIFO, determinism pair and reversal stress green, clippy -D warnings and fmt clean.

TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE SPEC, both flagged:

1. Spec item 1 said keep an arities() PROJECTION beside the shapes. Built as a DERIVED field inside TupleShapes instead -- exact(shapes) computes the arity set from the shapes' lengths -- so the coarse reading and the precise one are one fact rather than two that must be kept in step. arity_only(arities) carries the coarse case where no shape could be built. Same four oracle sites, one fewer invariant to police.

2. The measured predicate-lens canon move is 28 lines, not the 36 the spec quoted from the prototype. Same move (the narrow arm reseated first, arm/graph/plan lines only); the prototype's count came from a build without the envelope refinement and the delivered-fields repair.

TWO FINDINGS FILED:
- fz-kdt.140: the 2^arity per-position specialization product (the +42's cause); dbg/1 reads no position, so eight bodies differ in a type none of them projects. The review handed this to 'fz-3bb', which is not an issue in this tracker.
- fz-kdt.139: the fixture budget.* headers name counters nothing produces -- only budget.codegen.functions has a live producer, nothing enforces any of the ten, and receive_map_pattern read 26 against a measured 32 BEFORE this landing touched it.

Landed in-story per the gate list: fz-kdt.133 (repaired, and measured unreachable on today's corpus), fz-kdt.134 (folded), fz-kdt.135 (tripwire + baseline). fz-kdt.137 stays red and is why the nested-callable claim is gated by unit tests at the dispatch layer; its reproducer's error text moved, recorded there.

title: A tuple's runtime question is its positions: per-position sub-predicate shapes, identity-preserving erasure at every depth
